I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Using the same method, the Q2 calculation reproduced all 10 reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 value |
|---|---|
| a. Top-revenue segment / net sales | consumer / 287,348,307 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 244 |
| c. Top-revenue category / net sales | svc / 267,144,376 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u104@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 229 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 683,980 |
| h. Growth, August → September | -11.7% |

The DB has three data issues that I had to account for to reproduce the Q2 values:
- **Order times are stored in UTC** (`...Z`). The quarter and month boundaries only match the reference when converted to Korea time (UTC+9). Calculating in UTC gave different Q2 values (for example, a_net 237,940,457 and h 35.0).
- **Segment names are inconsistent**, for example `' consumer'` and `'Enterprise '`. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** 300 customer IDs share only 250 email addresses. Counting by ID gave b=273 and f=222 for Q2, which doesn't match. Counting one customer per email (trimmed, lowercased) gave the reference values of 235 and 196.

Refunds had no problems: every refund matches an order line, and no refund quantity exceeds the quantity ordered.

STATUS: DONE
